posts.caption: Yall mind if I get a little niche (surface Black Library lore) and yes in my headcanon Loken somehow survives and became an OG grey knight #warhammer40k #warhammer #hobby #40k #warhammer30k
posts.label: other
posts.worked: At 7.3 seconds with 245,869 views (41x median), the short run and the Black Library joke landed hard, and 18,662 likes (about 7.6% of views) is the strongest like rate in the set.
posts.didnt: Comments are thin at 229 (about 0.09% of views), and the caption leans on lore that only readers of the books will get, which runs against the account's non-player rule.
posts.next_time: Keep the 7-second length but turn the lore into his question as a newer player ("Is Loken an OG Grey Knight in your headcanon?"), which invites comments without making him the authority.

posts.worked: An 8-second meme about his own painting time (116,903 views, 19.5x median) is exactly the 'joke about his own hobby life' that reaches non-players, and it earned 7,686 likes.
posts.didnt: Comments are light at 61, and the caption carries the whole joke, so there is little story in the caption to give a viewer a reason to follow.
posts.next_time: Put the joke on screen and use the caption for one line of his story (e.g. what the 3 hours went on), so the post gives people a reason to follow.

posts.worked: A 15-second post about his own airbrushing (105,433 views, 17.6x median) with 7,620 likes shows a personal joke landing, and the viewer comment about the lights going crazy points to the lit model as the real draw.
posts.didnt: The label is meme, so the lit-model payoff is not being sold as the reason to watch, and the caption is only the joke with no craft hook.
posts.next_time: Keep the 15-second length and open on the lit model in second one, with the airbrush joke as the reaction over it, since the comment shows people came for the lights.

posts.caption: Somebody though they could sneak around and not get caught 🙄 #warhammer40k #warhammer #hobby #40k #alphalegion
posts.label: meme
posts.worked: The 8-second-to-13-second length is in the right range for a meme, and it got 62 likes at about 6.5% of views, so the few people who saw it liked it.
posts.didnt: At 956 views (0.2x median) with zero comments, it barely reached anyone. The #alphalegion joke is about a faction he doesn't play, not his minis or Guard army, so there's no reason for a non-player to care.
posts.next_time: Re-roll it as a joke about his own Guard army (e.g. his Guardsmen trying to sneak past the commissar), with his own audio and the payoff in second one.

posts.caption: A quick little demo on the LED’s! This may be one of my favorite parts of a build, and i definitely will be cramming electronics wherever I can now 😂 Let me know if you’d like to see a more in-depth explanation, or what
posts.label: craft
posts.worked: The LED demo has a lit-model payoff in its subject, and 176 likes at about 5.5% of views is a healthy like rate for a craft post.
posts.didnt: At 72.8 seconds it's far over the 30-second default and reads like a build log, with 3,178 views (0.5x median) and only one comment. The caption also asks whether people want more, which is a question the post should have answered in the first seconds.
posts.next_time: Cut it to about 15 seconds with the LED lighting up in second one, and move the 'how' to the caption or a follow-up post.

posts.caption: Magnets are awesome sauce. Lets me swap out loadouts, store my big guys more efficiently, and when needed take them apart to turn them into debris on the battlefield 😎 #warhammer40k #warhammer #hobby #40k #imperialknight
posts.label: craft
posts.worked: At 8.6 seconds it's the right length, and 177 likes (about 5.5% of views) show the like rate holds for craft.
posts.didnt: The caption explains a process (swapping loadouts, storing models) rather than showing a payoff, so a non-player has no reason to stop, and it reached only 3,224 views (0.5x median). The one comment is unrelated to the post.
posts.next_time: Open on the knight coming apart on the table as a kaiju-style reveal in second one, with a meme caption, instead of explaining the magnets.

patterns: Short posts about his own hobby life did best: the three strongest ran 7.3 to 15.2 seconds and reached 17.6x to 41.1x the window median, while the craft posts that ran long (72.8s) or explained a process (magnets) stayed near 0.5x.
Captions that name the joke or the feeling (the painting-time and airbrush posts) outperformed captions that carry insider references (#alphalegion, Loken lore), which fits the non-player rule.

Engagement per view was similar across formats (about 5% to 8%), so the difference between posts is reach, not how people react once they see them. The biggest gap is reach, which points to the opener and topic, and comments are very low across the window (mostly 0 to 2 per post).
